ex: The Worthens sighed with relief as the engine began its night of upgrade chugging.

senses.d: An improved component or replacement item, usually applied to technology.
ex: With my phone company, I get a free upgrade every twelve months if I keep topping up 10 pounds a month.
The remarried couples among my friends often joke that their divorce and remarriage amounted to an upgrade.

senses.d: To improve, usually applied to technology, generally by complete replacement of one or more components.
ex: When you upgrade your standard of living, you become addicted to that standard of living.
I had to upgrade my anti-virus software to protect my computer from the newer threats.

senses.d: To improve the equipment or furnishings of or services rendered to.
ex: They upgraded him to the latest model.
They were upgraded to first class.

senses.d: To improve in condition or status.
ex: She upgraded to a more successful husband.

senses.d: To replace a program with a later version of itself, a version having a higher version number or marketed under a more recent product name.
ex: She waited a long time to upgrade from Windows 10 to Windows 11, hoping the worst bugs would be worked out before she took the plunge.
She waited a long time to upgrade Windows, hoping the worst bugs would be worked out before she took the plunge.
Men fell out, worn-out, and there were sunstroke cases. It was an eight-mile march upgrade.
Northbound trains originating near the Ohio River faced a 26-mile climb upgrade to Flushing.

ety.text: Inherited from Late Latin meliōrāre, a verb based on Latin melior (“better”). By surface analysis, mejor + -ar. Compare English ameliorate.

pt:melhorar.gl: to improve, to ameliorate, to better
